chunks: If He, the Glorified, had willed to place His Sacred House and His great signs,
among gardens and rivers, and soft plains and level ground, full of trees, abundant with fruits, thick with buildings, connected with villages,
between golden wheat, and green gardens, and surrounding suburbs, and watered plains, and thriving orchards, and crowded streets,
the amount of recompense would have decreased because of the lightness of the trial.
ai.seo_question: Why is the reward for Hajj linked to the difficulty of the location?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) illustrates that the ascetic, arid nature of Mecca serves as a deliberate spiritual trial (balā'), ensuring that the reward for Hajj is proportional to the difficulty of the journey rather than the comfort of the destination. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that divine wisdom often places sacred sites in humble locations to test sincerity and detach believers from worldly allurements.

en.sayed-ali-raza: If Allāh, the Glorified, had placed His sacred House and His great signs
among plantations, streams, soft and level plains, plenty of trees, an abundance of fruits, a thick population, close habitats,
golden wheat, lush gardens, green land, watered plains, thriving orchards and crowded streets,
the amount of recompense would have decreased because of the lightness of the trial.
